questions.question_text: Find the scalar projection of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ in the direction of $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Dropped the sign of the dot product; a negative scalar projection means the shadow points opposite to $\underset{\sim}{b}$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 169$, which gives the scalar multiple for the vector projection, not the scalar projection.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{a}| = 5$ instead of by the magnitude of the vector being projected onto.
Ignored the direction of $\underset{\sim}{b}$; the projection must be a multiple of $-2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and the scalar $\frac{5}{2}$ is positive.
Projected onto the $x$-direction instead of onto $\underset{\sim}{b}$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 2$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 4$.

questions.question_text: $|\overrightarrow{OA}| = 12$ and $\angle AOB = 135^{\circ}$. Find the exact scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{OA}$ in the direction of $\overrightarrow{OB}$.

options.why: Used the acute supplement $45^{\circ}$, losing the negative sign that an obtuse angle produces.
Used $\cos 120^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}$ in place of $\cos 135^{\circ} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
Multiplied by $\sqrt{2}$ instead of $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, forgetting to halve.

questions.question_text: The points $A(0,1)$ and $B(8,7)$ are given. Find the projection of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{c} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Used $\overrightarrow{BA} = \begin{pmatrix} -8 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$ instead of $\overrightarrow{AB}$, reversing the sign of the dot product.
Projected $\underset{\sim}{c}$ onto $\overrightarrow{AB}$ instead of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{c}$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{c}| = \sqrt{5}$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{c}|^{2} = 5$.
Projected $\underset{\sim}{b}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{a}$, using $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2} = 14$ and the direction of $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 3$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 9$.
Used $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2} = 14$ in the denominator while still multiplying by $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

questions.question_text: The projection of $m\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j}$ onto $5\underset{\sim}{i}+12\underset{\sim}{j}$ has length $\dfrac{9}{13}$. Find all possible values of $m$.

options.why: Solved only $5m-36 = 9$ and ignored the second case $5m-36 = -9$ of the absolute value.
Set $5m-36$ equal to $\pm 9$ but then solved as if the $36$ were also negative.
Divided by $13$ a second time after the $13$s had already cancelled.
